subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool routing design now, or pause this PR until the broader federation identity and trust-boundary contract is decided?
rationale: This PR changes who a model-facing session tool may contact and which remote gateway can run sessions, so code review cannot safely choose the trust, identity, scope, and upgrade policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Pause for federation/security design
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and require an approved trust-boundary design before any core `gateway.peers` implementation lands.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow peer-config design
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept `gateway.peers` as the near-term scope, then require URL policy, idempotency, real spawn semantics, docs, tests, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Close this PR in favor of a replacement
options.body: If the current branch is too stale or too far from the desired contract, close it after a narrower maintainer-owned or ClawSweeper replacement path exists.

recommendation.title: Pause for federation/security design
recommendation.body: Keep the canonical issue open and require an approved trust-boundary design before any core `gateway.peers` implementation lands.

likelyOwner.reason: History ties this person to both the session-tool surface and the gateway URL hardening that this PR bypasses.
